Ralph was quick to remind Carl that the flock had honored the code of silence. A code of silence is an agreement that a flock honors when following one goose. From rooftops to busy streets to flying when it feels like your wings could snap. It doesn't matter. You follow the leader. While Carl complained, Ralph asked him to name the color of his clipboard. "Nice try, Ralph. That's a trick question. There is no clipboard," Carl said. Ralph leaned in and gently tapped his clipboard against Carl's beak. Carl, please get new glasses like we discussed. Though Carl pouted, Ralph continued down the line. He soon realized one goose was missing. "Where's Winston?" Ralph asked. "Betty," who stood at the other end of the line, said, "I know where Winston is." "Do you mind telling me where?" Ralph asked. Having promised she wouldn't say anything, Betty reluctantly agreed as Ralph pleaded that icicles were forming on his beak. Betty flew off the hilltop and the other geese followed her. "Okay, Betty, where's Winston?" Ralph asked. "It's not much further," Betty said. Betty led the flock down a riverbank and up a hill where an old wooded shed laid buried in brush. "Are you in there, Winston?" Betty asked. A loud noise from within the shed rattled its foundation. "Betty, is that you?" "Yes, it's her," Winston, Ralph said, shaking his head. We're ready to go. Winston was surprised to see the entire flock staring at him. What's everyone doing here, Betty? I asked you not to say anything. I'm sorry, Winston. We don't want to leave without you, Betty said. I can see that, but you're not a doctor, Winston. I know, Ralph, but the entire staff at the Birdfield Medical Clinic has already flown south. I feel for him, Ralph said, patting the little cardinal's head. But we've got to go. We can't stay here for the winter. I'm sorry, Ralph. I know it won't be easy, but I'm not leaving. Ralph began to speak, but interrupted himself with a loud sneeze. Well, as much as I disagree with Winston's decision, it's time to get underway, Ralph said, rubbing his beak. Ralph's cold presented a problem. Someone else would have to lead the flock. But the other members of the troop 408 were either past their prime or too inexperienced. Ralph would have to let Carl lead the flock. After the announcement, the members of Troop 408 consoled one another. Everyone pleaded with Winston to go, but he knew that taking care of his new friend was the right thing to do. The flock flew away, leaving Winston and the little cardinal all alone. #readaloud #interactivelearning #kidsstories 
Welcome to Safety Springs! In this interactive children's book, a curious little squirrel takes young readers on a journey through challenging scenarios where the reader is asked to make very important decisions. Covering themes of road safety, fire safety, stranger danger and more – Danger Buster is here to help. But instead of just telling kids what to do, Danger Buster asks them what they would do, encouraging them to think critically and make smart, safe choices.
Danger Buster is thoughtfully designed for children ages 3–5 and offers more than just a story, it’s a conversation starter. Each scenario dives into a real-world potentially dangerous situation, then pauses to ask the reader what the safest choice would be. It’s a fun and engaging way to build safety awareness and confidence to make safe decisions.
As a parent to two young children, the author was inspired to write Danger Buster to help teach her own kids how to navigate the world more safely. She wanted something more than a safety lecture, a playful and empowering way to teach important life lessons through storytelling, interaction, and imagination.
Whether you're a parent, teacher, or caregiver, this book opens the door to meaningful discussions with children about safety in a way that’s engaging, non-scary, fun and rewarding!

Rooty feels sad. Hearing the other vegetables laugh and play without him, the strange little rutabaga longs to be included. So when their catch-and-throw game tosses a nut his way, the lonely plant seizes his chance to meet new friends.

Confused at first by the curious pair of peppers who come across to retrieve their toy, Rooty accepts their invitation to join in the fun. But feeling awkward among the popular carrots and terrific tomatoes, he worries he doesn’t belong.
